idiom_name: Ktor call.principal<SubjectPrincipal>() with a typed authentication provider
implementation_notes: On Ktor the Authentication plugin is the mechanism: a provider validates the credential and returns a principal object that the call carries until the request completes, and consumers ask call.principal<SubjectPrincipal>() (optionally naming the provider). Define the descriptor as an immutable data class so equality, copies and destructuring behave, and use Ktor's type-safe authentication to bind principal types to providers instead of casting. In Spring-based Kotlin the same descriptor is Authentication.getPrincipal(), usually injected with @AuthenticationPrincipal; write your own descriptor only when the platform supplies none, and keep the credential outside it.
pitfalls: call.principal<T>() returns null both when the route is unauthenticated and when the type or provider does not match - a non-null assertion turns that into a 500; guard the route with authenticate(...) and fail closed.
Principal data classes with var fields or MutableList attributes let later code mutate the identity; use immutable collections and val.
Several providers (basic, bearer, session) can produce different principal types for the same call; query the intended provider explicitly instead of assuming the first one.
